item.title: Windows Server 2028 Preview drops VBScript, WINS and SMBv1 — 19 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 November 2026

Windows Server 2028 Preview drops VBScript, WINS and SMBv1

The most consequential updates define a stricter Windows Server 2028 Preview compatibility baseline: VBScript, WINS, and SMBv1 are removed, while Hyper-V guidance directs administrators to use Generation 2 guests and UEFI-capable physical hosts. Separately, Windows Server 2025 makes WMIC available as a Feature on Demand installed with DISM.

Administration · Command reference

VBScript is removed from Windows Server 2028 Preview

The Cscript guidance now says Windows Server 2025 includes VBScript as a Feature on Demand, but Windows Server 2028 Preview removes it. Cscript cannot run scripts requiring the VBScript engine on that release, while Windows Script Host and JScript remain available. Migrate VBScript automation to PowerShell and test before deployment.

DNS and DHCP · General

WINS gives way to DNS in the 2028 Preview

WINS remains supported throughout the Windows Server 2025 lifecycle but has been removed from Windows Server 2028 Preview. The updated guidance adds direction for replacing WINS with DNS, so WINS-dependent organizations should plan the transition and decommissioning work.

Storage · General

SMBv1 cannot be restored on Windows Server 2028 Preview

The updated availability guidance says Windows Server 2028 Preview no longer includes SMBv1 and cannot install or enable it. Windows Server 2019 through 2025 still omit SMBv1 by default, but SMBv1-dependent systems must be updated or replaced before a 2028 Preview upgrade.

Hyper-V · General

Hyper-V guidance shifts 2028 Preview deployments to Generation 2

The updated Hyper-V guidance recommends Generation 2 VMs for Windows Server 2028 Preview and planning for UEFI firmware on physical Hyper-V hosts running that version. Support for earlier guest operating systems is unchanged.

Administration · Command reference

WMIC becomes an installable Feature on Demand in Server 2025

The WMIC reference now states that WMIC is available as a Feature on Demand beginning with Windows Server 2025 and adds a DISM installation instruction. Administrators who need WMIC must add the Feature on Demand rather than assume it is present.

View all updates for 19 November 2026 →

item.title: Windows Server 2028 Preview flags WINS, SMBv1 and WSUS for deprecation or removal — 18 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 18 November 2026

Windows Server 2028 Preview flags WINS, SMBv1 and WSUS for deprecation or removal

The period's most consequential update is the Windows Server 2028 Preview inventory of features deprecated or removed, including WINS, DirectAccess, SMBv1, VBScript, WMIC, WSUS, legacy BIOS, BranchCache, WDS, and PowerShell 5.1. The preview documentation cautions that plans may change. Microsoft also added preview guidance for SMB Policy Controller, narrowed Network HUD deployment guidance, and standardized Windows Server Token factory endpoint terminology in Local AI procedures.

Windows Server · General

Windows Server 2028 Preview enumerates a broad legacy-feature retirement list

The preview page now lists WINS, DirectAccess, SMBv1, VBScript, WMIC, WSUS, legacy BIOS, BranchCache, WDS, and PowerShell 5.1 among deprecated or removed features, while noting that plans may change before release. Administrators should inventory dependencies and plan alternatives such as DNS, Always On VPN, SMBv2/v3, PowerShell, or UEFI where applicable.

Storage · General

SMB Policy Controller preview adds intent-based server and share reconciliation

New guidance describes SMB Policy Controller managing and correcting server-wide and share-level SMB intents through configuration, verification, troubleshooting, and removal workflows. The preview requires Windows Server Insider Preview build 29707 or later and installation of the PolicyController Feature on Demand.

Networking · Planning and deployment

Network HUD guidance narrows installation scope to physical Azure Arc clusters

The installation article now targets Azure Arc-enabled Windows Server 2025 Datacenter physical clusters with at least two nodes. It adds prerequisites for Hyper-V, Network ATC, Storage Spaces Direct, DCB/LLDP, validated switches, Azure permissions, and Windows Admin Center, while stating that virtual machines and offline installation are unsupported.

Local AI · General

Token factory endpoint guidance adds concrete client connectivity prerequisites

The Local AI procedure now covers connecting a Windows client to an existing Windows Server Token factory endpoint, removes same-device scenarios, and requires network reachability, DNS, trusted TLS, and HTTPS. Administrators following the procedure should use the updated endpoint model and prerequisites.

View all updates for 18 November 2026 →

item.title: Windows Admin Center guidance splits modes and warns pre-2611 upgrades require re-registration — 17 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 17 November 2026

Windows Admin Center guidance splits modes and warns pre-2611 upgrades require re-registration

Microsoft Learn’s Windows Admin Center guidance now clearly separates Administration Mode from Virtualization Mode across installation, access, Hyper-V onboarding, clustering, networking, and virtual-machine procedures. The revised material also documents a significant version 2611 registration caveat, while Hyper-V Replica pages remove preview wording and the standalone Virtualization Mode preview installation article is removed.

Management · Planning and deployment

Virtualization Mode installation now has explicit hardware and lifecycle requirements

The main installation article now documents both Administration Mode and Virtualization Mode, including interactive and command-line setup. Virtualization Mode requires a dedicated server with at least 4 cores, 8 GB of RAM, and 10 GB of disk space; changing modes later requires reinstallation.

Management · General

Hyper-V resource onboarding gains a detailed prerequisites checklist

The updated article covers creating resource groups and onboarding standalone Hyper-V hosts or clusters. Administrators are directed to check roles, host capacity, supported Windows Server versions, domain and DNS configuration, connectivity, firewall rules, and exclusive management before onboarding resources.

Management · General

Version 2611 guidance adds a gateway re-registration requirement after upgrades

The Administration Mode article now says version 2611 can register a gateway with Azure RBAC without creating a custom Microsoft Entra application. Upgrades from before version 2611 do not preserve the existing registration: the gateway is unregistered and users are signed out, so administrators must re-register it and select a registration model with its prerequisites.

Management · Fundamentals

Virtualization Mode networking guidance limits template changes to future deployments

The Virtualization Mode overview now states that hyperconverged storage configuration is unavailable and that editing a network intent template affects only future deployments. Existing Network ATC intents must instead be managed with Network ATC PowerShell cmdlets.

Hyper-V · General

Hyper-V Replica guidance removes its Virtualization Mode preview notice

The Hyper-V Replica failover-cluster guidance no longer labels configuration through Windows Admin Center’s Virtualization mode as preview software subject to change. The update changes the page’s qualification and wording without stating a new availability milestone.

View all updates for 17 November 2026 →

item.title: DNS Server adds Event 506 and relocates debug logs outside its default directory — 14 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 14 November 2026

DNS Server adds Event 506 and relocates debug logs outside its default directory

The period’s most consequential guidance concerns DNS logging and Windows Admin Center compatibility. Applicable 2026 cumulative updates are documented as logging DNS Event ID 506 and relocating existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`; changing `LogFilePath` now requires local Administrators membership. Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 is documented as moving to .NET 10, with Azure Connected Machine Agent 1.65 or earlier unable to upgrade to that version or later. Failover Cluster Manager guidance also tightens the campus-cluster procedure around KB5072033, the fault-domain property, and storage-pool version.

DNS and DHCP · PowerShell and automation

DNS guidance documents new logging and permission behavior

Starting with applicable 2026 cumulative updates, DNS Server logs Event ID 506 and relocates existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`. Changing `LogFilePath` requires membership in local Administrators; DnsAdmins membership alone is denied.

Management · Releases, upgrades and migration

Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 moves to .NET 10

The 1.3.0.0 release upgrades Windows Admin Center to .NET 10. Azure Connected Machine Agent version 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to this Windows Admin Center version or later versions.

Management · General

Arc agent guidance preserves connection and upgrade boundaries

The Arc hybrid-machine guidance states that agent versions 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to Windows Admin Center 1.0.0.0 or later. It also records that Arc agent versions 1.35 and 1.36 break Windows Admin Center connections, while version 1.37 and later fix that issue.

Failover Clustering · General

Campus-cluster instructions revise the fault-domain and storage prerequisites

The Failover Cluster Manager procedure now scopes KB5072033 to every server joining the cluster, replaces `FaultDomainAwareness` checks with `FaultDomainAwarenessDefault`, and clarifies the requirement for storage pool version 29 or later.

View all updates for 14 November 2026 →

item.title: RD Web Access XSLT customizations face Chromium M158 cutoff November 17, 2026 — 13 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 November 2026

RD Web Access XSLT customizations face Chromium M158 cutoff November 17, 2026

New Remote Desktop guidance covers assessing, migrating, validating, and troubleshooting RD Web Access customizations that rely on browser-native XSLT. Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT beginning November 17, 2026.

Remote Desktop · Releases, upgrades and migration

Migration path added for RD Web Access XSLT customizations

The guidance explains how to assess, migrate, validate, and troubleshoot customizations using browser-native XSLT. It directs administrators to keep the updated .aspx pages unchanged and configure a separate stylesheet through RDWebSiteXsltPath before Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT on November 17, 2026.

item.title: AD FS FAQ ties unknown domain identifiers to controller discovery and CLDAP safeguards — 12 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 12 November 2026

AD FS FAQ ties unknown domain identifiers to controller discovery and CLDAP safeguards

An updated AD FS troubleshooting FAQ explains that unrecognized domain identifiers in username and password requests can trigger domain controller discovery, including DNS SRV queries and CLDAP pings. It recommends Extranet Smart Lockout on Windows Server 2019 and later, along with restricting outbound CLDAP traffic.

AD FS · Troubleshooting

AD FS guidance details domain-controller discovery triggered by unknown identifiers

The FAQ says unrecognized domain identifiers in username and password requests can initiate domain controller discovery through DNS SRV queries and CLDAP pings. It recommends Extranet Smart Lockout for Windows Server 2019 and later and restricting outbound CLDAP traffic.

item.title: SID-bearing certificate requests: NDES guidance explains SAN, extension, and custom policy-module exception — 11 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 11 November 2026

SID-bearing certificate requests: NDES guidance explains SAN, extension, and custom policy-module exception

The 11 November batch was largely documentation maintenance, with the most substantive update in AD CS. NDES guidance now covers certificate requests carrying SID information in the SAN or a separate SID extension, including the custom policy module exception. Other meaningful edits refresh VM conversion links for VDDK 8.0.3 and Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting, while Active Directory and AD FS received narrower reference and wording updates.

AD CS · General

NDES guidance details SID data in SANs and separate certificate extensions

The AD CS article now describes NDES behavior for requests containing SID information in the SAN or in a separate SID extension, including the exception for custom policy modules. Administrators working on affected enrollment scenarios should consult this guidance during design or troubleshooting.

Management · Releases, upgrades and migration

VM conversion guidance links directly to Broadcom for VDDK 8.0.3

The migration procedure now points to Broadcom Support for downloading VMware VDDK 8.0.3. The required version and extraction path remain unchanged, so the practical action is to use the updated download link.

Management · Troubleshooting

Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting now uses a new Broadcom guide URL

The VM conversion troubleshooting article now links to a new Broadcom VDDK Programming Guide URL for Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting. Administrators following the article will be directed to that updated resource.

Active Directory · General

Active Directory security guidance now links to OWASP’s 2025 Top 10

The Avenues To Compromise article replaces its former OWASP index link with the OWASP 2025 Top 10 page, directing readers to current vulnerability and countermeasure information. No configuration change is required.

AD FS · General

AD FS smart-lockout guidance revises proxy request wording and metadata

The AD FS extranet smart lockout article received updated DevRel metadata links and a minor revision describing ESL requests through Web Application Proxy or an MS-ADFSPIP-compatible third-party proxy. No administrator action is indicated.

View all updates for 11 November 2026 →

item.title: NDES guidance adds SID certificate request settings and validation safeguards — 7 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 November 2026

NDES guidance adds SID certificate request settings and validation safeguards

A new AD CS article explains how to configure NDES to accept SID information in certificate requests through registry settings for SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats.

AD CS · General

New AD CS guidance covers SID-enabled NDES requests

The article documents registry configuration for accepting SID information in certificate requests, including SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats. It advises that a trusted component validate the SID before enabling these settings and specifies resetting IIS or restarting NDES to apply changes.

View all updates for 7 November 2026 →
